Regarding the encryption method mentioned in the content, the paragraph itself provides a reasonable assessment of its current effectiveness. It correctly identifies that while Quantum-Resistant Encryption is designed to be secure against future quantum computing threats, its practical effectiveness in the current landscape is difficult to measure because large-scale, functional quantum computers are not yet widely available. Therefore, the method is theoretically robust for future threats but lacks empirical validation in the present day due to the absence of the specific threat environment (i.e., powerful quantum computers) it is designed to counter.
